analysis:
Examined the complete base/head test script and patch. scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py replaces dispatch-only, credential-free ad-hoc build assertions and master-only publication assertions (base 31–100) with assertions for a dev-push reusable workflow, inherited secrets and write permissions (head 97–170), Apple signing-secret placement and guarded environment secrets (180–199), Developer ID/notarization and fan-helper identity verification (201–213), and serialized dev publication (215–221). The script reads workflow text and performs assertions; it does not itself build, sign, publish, access credentials or alter provider runtime behavior. No independently supported vulnerability is established in this test-only scope. Prompt encryption, cache isolation (T-041), billing, cancellation and local hold controls are not changed here.
The intended release-lane change is material to A-005, A-011, A-017, T-013, T-034, T-054 and the TB-010 helper identity contract. Integration must inspect .github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml, release-provider.yml and release-swift.yml to verify actual source selection, version stamping, secret availability and execution during build/sign/publication. Head 138 explicitly expects secrets: inherit; absence of named secrets in the caller is not evidence of credential isolation. Head 180–199 checks expression spelling and job placement, not whether branch-controlled build scripts execute with signing credentials or whether dev artifacts can enter production qualification. The workflows and branch authorization controls are not supplied, so these remain unverified contracts rather than findings. Reconcile this new signing scope with the canonical distinction between signed artifacts and independently qualified serving authorization.
